<p class="eyebrow">Experimental desktop builds</p>

# Download LinkEDA

LinkEDA is available as a native desktop application for macOS and Windows.
Choose the edition for your operating system and R setup. All builds are
experimental, so keep copies of important data and verify consequential
analyses from the exported R recipe.

## macOS {#download}

The current macOS build is **LinkEDA 0.0.120** for **Apple Silicon** (M1 or
newer) and **macOS 14 or later**. Choose the option that matches how you work:

- **Already use R or RStudio:** the R binary package is usually the most
  convenient option. It installs into your R library and does not require
  Apple's application notarisation or the **Open Anyway** approval.
- **Want a self-contained application:** choose the Standalone edition. It
  includes its own R runtime.
- **Want an application that uses your installed R:** choose the System R
  edition. It requires Apple Silicon R 4.6.

The two application editions install `LinkEDA.app` in the Applications folder.
Installing one application edition replaces the other.

### Standalone edition

::: {.download-card}
<img src="assets/LinkEDA.png" alt="LinkEDA application icon.">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Self-contained application · macOS arm64 · about 298 MB</p>
<p>Includes a private R 4.6 runtime and the packages used by LinkEDA. Choose
this edition when you want a self-contained application; an existing R
installation is not required.</p>
<p><a class="button button-primary" href="https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/releases/download/v0.0.120-macOS/LinkEDA-0.0.120-macOS-arm64-Standalone.pkg">Download standalone installer</a></p>
</div>
:::

#### Install the Standalone edition

1. Close LinkEDA if an older version is running.
2. Open `LinkEDA-0.0.120-macOS-arm64-Standalone.pkg` and complete the installer.
3. Open **LinkEDA** from the Applications folder.
4. If macOS says that it cannot verify the developer, close that message and
   open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**.
5. Under **Security**, find the message saying that LinkEDA or its installer
   was blocked and choose **Open Anyway** (or **Abrir igualmente**).
6. Authenticate with your password or Touch ID and choose **Open**. If the
   installer was blocked, run it again after approval. If installation
   succeeds but the application is blocked at first launch, repeat the same
   approval for `LinkEDA.app`.

This edition is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarised by
Apple, which is why macOS may request the one-time approval. You do not need to
disable Gatekeeper. Control-clicking the installer or application and choosing
**Open** may also display the approval directly.

### R binary package

::: {.download-card}
<img src="assets/LinkEDA.png" alt="LinkEDA application icon.">
<div>
<p class="eyebrow">Recommended for current R users · macOS arm64 · about 8.3 MB</p>
<p>Installs LinkEDA in an existing Apple Silicon R 4.6 library. Use this
edition when you already work in R or RStudio. It is the smallest download and
does not install a separate application or macOS installer.</p>
<p><a class="button button-primary" href="https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/releases/download/v0.0.120-macOS/LinkEDA_0.0.120.tgz">Download R package</a></p>
</div>
:::

#### Install the R binary package

**No Apple notarisation or Gatekeeper approval is needed for this option.** It
is installed and started from R or RStudio, so the **Privacy & Security > Open
Anyway** steps used by the two application installers do not apply.

The package requires Apple Silicon R 4.6 and macOS 14 or later. In R or the
RStudio Console, install the required packages and then LinkEDA:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "digest", "effectsize", "statmod", "withr", "janitor",
  "later", "mice", "miceadds", "psych"
))

install.packages(
  "https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/releases/download/v0.0.120-macOS/LinkEDA_0.0.120.tgz",
  repos = NULL,
  type = "binary"
)

library(LinkEDA)
LinkEDA()
```

You can instead download the `.tgz` and select it in RStudio through **Tools >
Install Packages > Install from: Package Archive File**. Install the required
packages in the first command before selecting the archive. Features that use
optional R packages report what else is needed when you open them.

</div>

#### Install the System R edition

1. Confirm that Apple Silicon R 4.6 is installed, then close LinkEDA if an
   older version is running.
2. Open `LinkEDA-0.0.120-macOS-arm64-System-R.pkg` and complete the installer.
3. Open **LinkEDA** from the Applications folder.
4. If macOS says that it cannot verify the developer, close that message and
   open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**.
5. Under **Security**, find the message saying that LinkEDA or its installer
   was blocked and choose **Open Anyway** (or **Abrir igualmente**).
6. Authenticate with your password or Touch ID and choose **Open**. If the
   installer was blocked, run it again after approval. If installation
   succeeds but the application is blocked at first launch, repeat the same
   approval for `LinkEDA.app`.

This edition is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID or notarised by
Apple, which is why macOS may request the one-time approval. You do not need to
disable Gatekeeper. The application reports the R requirement at launch if a
compatible installation cannot be found.

<p>Uses an existing installation of R 4.1 or newer and installs LinkEDA in

<p><a class="button button-primary" href="https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/releases/download/v0.0.113R/Instalar-LinkEDA-0.0.113-Windows.exe">Download standard installer</a></p>

Both Windows installers create a **LinkEDA** shortcut on the desktop. Neither
requires Rtools, Visual Studio or Windows Developer Mode. Internet access is
required while the required R packages are installed.

### Windows checksums

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| Complete installer | `9427D998EEFB6028B9B671CF6C6DC5564F77856F8753A2DFA4622FEEF9591516` |
| Standard installer | `55AA9C5BD2019589ADE97863CF73FECEC784BCF8ECBA2CA10AF351E0F1301832` |

### Install and start on Windows

1. Close LinkEDA if an older version is running.
2. Double-click the downloaded installer.
3. Wait while it installs LinkEDA and the required R packages.
4. Open **LinkEDA** from the desktop shortcut.

Running a newer installer updates an existing installation; uninstalling the
previous version is not required. Windows may show a reputation warning because
the experimental installers are not code signed. Check the filename and
SHA-256 value before running the file.

## Start with data

The Welcome window can import a supported data file or open an included
example. The editions that use an installed R can also start from an R data
frame:

```r
library(LinkEDA)
LinkEDA(mtcars)
```

The standalone macOS and complete Windows editions run their own private R
session behind the desktop application.

## Report a problem

Report bugs through the [LinkEDA issue tracker on
GitHub](https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/issues). Include the LinkEDA version,
operating-system version, installer edition and the steps that triggered the
problem. Do not attach confidential data; use a small anonymous example when
data are needed to reproduce the problem.
